persona: Commercial and Merchandising Planner. I own bookings, gross margin, inventory liability and channel mix for Basketball Apparel. I am not scoring how interesting an idea is; I am scoring whether I could put it on a buy sheet, price it on a ladder rung that holds, reorder it, and not own it at 50 percent off in September. Proven demand, a defensible price rung, low cannibalisation, a clear cost-to-make and a replenishable SKU shape score well. Anecdotal evidence, unpriced innovation, dated non-replenishable capsules and door-level extended size runs score badly. Risk in my column is execution and inventory risk first, demand risk second.
narrative:
I ranked this portfolio the way I would build a buy sheet, and the order is close to the inverse of how exciting the briefs read. Four of the eight proposed a new price rung. None anchored it to a retrieved page, the audit found three incompatible Nike ladders, and every observable shelf is discounting - DNA 8 in at 50 percent off, Sabrina's USD 65 clearing at USD 42.97, the Australian UV Woven at AUD 44.99 against a AUD 75-80 ask. In a business growing +2 percent currency-neutral on units +1 percent (A03-S9), an unanchored price-up is not upside; it is a markdown I have not booked yet. So I rewarded ideas that make money without asking the consumer to pay more, and marked down every case that closes on ASP.

That rule built the top. OPP-03 wins because it is the only proposal that creates margin without creating inventory: no new SKU, no new colour library, price held, funded by deleting a liner that rules make redundant (A06-S3, A06-S6). It carries the highest adjusted confidence (48) and two kill attempts that failed outright. OPP-02 takes the second INVEST on readiness, not score - the challenger cut it to 40, then said it would fund the de-scoped version. I agree: ladder a garment that already ships, hold price, and never buy the certification moat that failed live retrieval (AATCC 183 and ASTM D6603 already cover wet and stretched).

OPP-07 is where I overrode myself. The demand is the strongest untouched evidence here - the challenger took 20 points off and could not weaken it - and Nike holds the exclusive licence on both halves of the outfit. But the fixture the brief calls the opportunity already exists, stocked with Nike product at USD 74.99-84.99, so the honest ask is a block input and a wall adjacency measured against sell-through Nike already owns - not a franchise with an unbuyable six-dimensional SKU matrix. EXPLORE, below two lower-scoring ideas.

The bottom is where I diverge most from adjusted confidence. OPP-06 scores higher on confidence (39) than OPP-05 (24) or OPP-01 (26) and still lands near them, because confidence measures whether a brief is true; I measure whether it is buyable. A dated, non-replenishable capsule priced above a ladder already clearing at 25-50 percent off, inside a FIBA position expiring in 2027, with LA28 merchandise at Fanatics and 3x3 apparel at FOURTEEN, is the worst inventory shape in the file - scalability 1, risk 1. OPP-01 and OPP-05 fail one test from opposite ends: OPP-01 proposes SKUs Nike already sells at team net above its own street price; OPP-05 proposes a EUR 45 rung that likely de-rates live European business and duplicates two better-evidenced briefs.

Preserving the disagreement: OPP-08 is the only brief with no fatal kill and I may be wrong to rank it fourth. What would move this ranking most is not research - it is the internal price-file and realised-ASP pull six of these eight briefs are waiting on.
weighting_rationale: Weights, and why they are not equal. COMMERCIAL POTENTIAL 18 percent - the portfolio's founding financial fact is that Nike apparel grew +2 percent currency-neutral on units +1 percent (A03-S9), so growth is mix and price, not volume; an idea that cannot show where the incremental margin dollar comes from is not an opportunity, it is a project. EVIDENCE STRENGTH 15 percent - the cross-dataset audit is blunt that there is no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base, that not one price or spec claim was confirmed against a retrieved page, and that three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist. In that environment I pay a premium for signals that are audited disclosure, primary rule text or peer-reviewed physiology, and I discount everything sourced from report mills. RISK 14 percent, and I score it as EXECUTION AND INVENTORY risk, not demand risk - a great idea in a non-replenishable dated capsule, a 12-colour library, or a door-level full size run is a markdown event with a good story on it. SCALABILITY 12 percent - I reward actions that ride an existing block, carry over, and reorder; I punish single-market proving grounds and SKU matrices that multiply out past what any buyer will place. MARKET WHITESPACE 10 percent and PRODUCT DIFFERENTIATION 9 percent are deliberately mid-weighted, because the single most repeated failure in this pipeline is a specialist declaring white space that Nike or a competitor already occupies; the audit says the base's errors are almost entirely negative claims that something does not exist. CONSUMER NEED 8 percent - real, but in this base need is almost never sized, and an unsized need cannot be bought against. NIKE RIGHT TO WIN 7 percent. BASKETBALL AUTHENTICITY 4 percent and CULTURAL RELEVANCE 3 percent are the lowest weights and I want that on the record as a disagreement with the brand lens, not an oversight: authenticity and culture are licences to enter, not reasons to book units, and every idea here is authentically basketball. I used the challenger's adjusted confidence as the ceiling discipline on evidence_strength and risk, not as the score itself - adjusted confidence measures whether the brief is true, while my overall measures whether the business is worth buying. That is why OPP-03 (adj 48) outranks OPP-08 (adj 44) by more than four points, and why OPP-06 (adj 39) sits below OPP-05 and OPP-01's neighbours on risk despite a higher adjusted confidence than both.

scores.rationale: Highest adjusted confidence in the portfolio (60 -> 48) and by a distance the best shape for my P&L. This is the only idea here that creates margin without creating inventory: no new SKU, no new colour library, no new price rung, price explicitly held (Icon 6/8 in USD 30, Icon 11 in USD 35, DNA 8 in USD 65). The return is markdown avoidance on the two franchises that already carry men's basketball shorts unit volume, in a business where units are +1 percent and every dollar of growth is mix (A03-S9). Two of the challenger's twelve kill attempts failed outright - the consumer need and the causal premise - and the defect reproduced independently on two Icon inseams across three retail venues, which is more corroboration than the base originally credited (A01-S3, A04-S6; 3.9 stars, 67 percent recommending across 64 reviews). The liner deletion is the funding mechanism and it is rules-clean: compression under the short is legal at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6), so the densest wet mass in the garment comes out and pays for the seam and shrinkage spec. I accept two fatal findings and neither touches the programme. The 20-wash badge fails its own job story - a season of weekly washing exceeds 20 cycles and contract sourcing treats 100-plus as normal for team mesh - so the badge does not ship. The lifetime-style guarantee is a documented loss-maker across every scaled precedent (L.L.Bean, REI, Dr Martens) and is redundant against EMEA's two-year statutory guarantee, so the guarantee does not ship either. What ships is a make standard and a buy discipline: fewer colourways, deeper, replenishment with a guaranteed reorder window. I also own the challenger's sharpest commercial correction as my own error to fix - the USD 19 recovery is modelled at RETAIL inside a 70/30 wholesale-weighted programme, so a meaningful share of it is a gift to Dick's and Foot Locker, not Nike margin. That is a re-model at Nike realised revenue, two to three weeks of analyst time at zero external cost, and it is the gate. Every validation step uses data Nike already owns.
scores.biggest_risk: The business case is booked at the wrong P&L level and may not survive being rebuilt at Nike realised wholesale revenue - if the recovered markdown mostly accrues to the retailer, the programme becomes a cost with a trust benefit and no payback. Secondary and structurally harder: Nike does not own the factories, so a 20-plus-cycle seam and dimensional-stability spec has to be enforced through tier-2 suppliers on a USD 30 garment already absorbing roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and a 120bp FY26 gross-margin headwind (A04-S8), and the shrinkage half of the diagnosis is substantially a high-heat-drying artifact no construction spec can reach.

scores.rationale: The demand floor here is the strongest untouched evidence in the whole base and the challenger says so explicitly - it took 20 points off (61 -> 41) and could not lay a finger on the demand half: three consecutive record seasons on a per-game basis, an All-Star crowd outdrawing the NBA's, 73 million unique viewers at the halfway mark, a ratified seven-year CBA with the cap up roughly fivefold, VERIFIED Unrivaled economics including a Philadelphia night at roughly USD 1M in tickets plus USD 400,000 in merchandise (A05-S7), a VERIFIED wholesale swing (A02-S7) and a first-party retailer call-out (A04-S5). Nike also holds the exclusive licence on BOTH halves of the outfit, and 'Nike's right to win with this specific consumer' was one of the few kill attempts that failed outright. That is the fastest-growing demand pool anywhere in this portfolio and I want money in it. I am not funding THIS brief, for two reasons I score hard. First, the fixture premise - the stated kill condition, 'the fixture IS the opportunity' - is met in the wrong direction: the fan-bottoms fixture already exists, is already stocked, and is stocked with NIKE. Fanatics runs a Ladies WNBA Shorts category carrying Nike Legends Flow Mesh at USD 74.99, On-Court Victory at USD 84.99 and Logowoman Crossover at USD 49.99; Nike's own WNBA pages carry Victory knee-length at USD 85; Rebel Fanwear shorts have been in fan doors since 8 May 2026. So the incremental ask collapses from a franchise to a block-and-proportion input plus a merchandising adjacency - which is cheap, and which I would fund. Second, the price is indefensible as argued: USD 65-75 rests entirely on a fan-wall comparison set that is itself discounting 25-45 percent with codes, and the observed women's rung (Sabrina USD 65) was found clearing at USD 42.97. As a planner I also cannot buy the specced SKU matrix - two fabrics x two inseams x XS-3X-plus-tall x four core colours x three drop windows x per-tour-stop exclusives is an unbuyable size curve and a guaranteed broken assortment. The decisive test is the challenger's, not the brief's, and it is better and nearly free: Nike already owns Rebel Fanwear and Caitlin Clark shorts sell-through, which measures this exact thesis in-market with no vendor and no field cost, in two to three weeks.
scores.biggest_risk: Buying a franchise into a fixture Nike already occupies - the realistic outcome is that the new block cannibalises Victory, Crossover, Sabrina and Rebel Fanwear rather than adding units, while the SKU matrix breaks the size curve and the USD 65-75 rung marks down to the USD 43-53 the neighbouring walls are already clearing at. The evidence risk beneath that: the whole bottom-half thesis rests on an inference the auditor told the base to discard, that 'female jersey outfit' at +494 percent implies demand for a bottom - on the same report that returned F1 at +483 percent and Brazil jersey at +302 percent.

scores.rationale: I am splitting this idea in two and funding the cheap half now. The challenger cut it 62 -> 40 and then said the quiet part out loud: the de-scoped version - rename and ladder the existing FN2659 DNA UV Woven block, add a knee-clearing 9-inch and a boys' 5-inch, fix hangtag legibility, hold price - is 'high-confidence, cheap, and I would fund it.' So would I, and I would book it against the SS28 assortment rather than a development budget, because it needs no research gate: the garment exists, is already globally distributed, is already stocked at the named doors, and the change is a merchandising and ladder action with essentially zero incremental inventory liability. That is why it earns INVEST at an overall four points below OPP-07 - category here reflects readiness to act, not just score. The consumer need is the strongest cross-domain corroboration in the portfolio and it survived direct attack: A06-S2 (VERIFIED physiology), A06-S5 (documented institutional behaviour change) and A03-S7 (Li-Ning's multi-season Wade UPF 50+ commercial platform) share no source and converge. The channel logic is audited - wholesale +4 percent against ten consecutive quarters of Nike Digital decline (A02-S7, A04-S1) - and 65/35 wholesale-led is the correct inversion. What I am NOT funding is the version that made it a Council item. Two fatal findings: the 'first to certify wet and stretched' differentiator is not a first - AATCC 183 already provides a wet test status and ASTM D6603 already conditions specimens for stretch, so it is a purchasable test election Li-Ning can answer in one cycle, not a moat - and USD 55 / AUD 75-80 is contradicted by the shelves the spec itself names: DNA 8 in at 50 percent off, DNA 6 in realised at USD 37.50, the UV Woven at AUD 44.99 against a AUD 75-80 ask. Strip the ASP-accretive lever and this is not a price-up, it is a findability and ladder fix, which is a perfectly good use of my money. Also unbuyable as written: per-colourway UPF certification is economically incompatible with the seasonal local-graphic strategy the same brief proposes.
scores.biggest_risk: That the organisation funds the expensive half. If certification is treated as the moat and USD 55 as the rung, I own per-colourway test cost against a feature NORTHYARD already ships on Amazon at UPF 50+ in 5/7/9 inseams, unlined and zip-pocketed, and a price the shelf has already refused. Secondary commercial risk: this is a franchise EXTENSION of the block it sits on, so it replaces rather than adds unless the ladder is planned with the DNA 6-inch explicitly - and the lead-market question is unresolved, with SS28 pointing at Greater China while the base holds not one Chinese price or sell-through datum.

scores.rationale: The only opportunity in the portfolio with no fatal kill - ten 'weakens' and two attacks that failed outright - and I weight that, because in this pipeline the recurring failure mode is a fatal 'Nike already ships this.' But the headline is confounded and I have to say so: retrieving Nike UK shows the price gap is mostly DNA versus DNA Academy at constant length (GBP 20) rather than length at constant franchise (GBP 12), so the 'ladder inversion' is roughly a third of the claimed size. And the length rung the brief says it is creating already exists inside the premium franchise - DNA 8 in at USD 55, 10 in at USD 50 - which fails the NEW test this engine exists to enforce. What genuinely survives is narrow, verified and damning in exactly the way a merchant should care about: Nike offers no premium-make basketball short in extended sizes in the biggest big-and-tall door, only its two cheapest franchises, one of which carries a seam-failure review corpus (A02-S5, A04-S6) - which is the same defect OPP-03 is chartered to fix, so the two should be run together. Extended sizes are also a low-competitive-intensity pool where AND1 to 5XL at USD 9.98 is the only real alternative. The two attacks that failed cut both ways and I keep them visible: the demand-side timing genuinely runs against the long end, and the AND1 buyer is a price buyer who will not move to USD 55 - realised Nike price at Kohl's is USD 27.75 today, so the ask is nearly double, not half again, with no willingness-to-pay evidence anywhere in the base or on the open web. The auditor's finding that no unit share by inseam exists protects the brief as much as it indicts it. Fund the challenger's de-scope: a two-week internal price-file decomposition at zero external cost, then one 11-inch inside the premium franchise for one season. Do not fund an architecture.
scores.biggest_risk: The load-bearing decision - a full size run at one price across physical doors - has a documented door-level failure precedent in Old Navy BODEQUALITY, which retrenched within nine months for precisely the reason I would cite: over-planned large sizes and excess inventory. Extended-size door distribution is the single most reliable way to break a size curve and end the season owning the tails, and no unit share by inseam or by size exists anywhere in this evidence base to plan the buy against. Hold the full run on nike.com and prove door-level demand before it is bought.

scores.rationale: Best-evidenced non-US market in the base, wrong programme wrapped around it - the challenger's phrase is 'real market, wrong programme' and I agree at 61 -> 38. What survives is genuinely good and I score evidence_strength at 4 for it: A04-S3 and A02-S7 are VERIFIED corporate disclosure, A05-S6 verifies verbatim against the NBL's own release, and the NBL27 dates (19 Sep 2026 to 14 Feb 2027) check exactly. Nike already ships the garment into Rebel's roughly 163 doors, which makes the cheap version nearly free. What kills it as a standalone line item is arithmetic that is squarely my discipline: the spec stakes everything on reading Australia BEFORE the SS28 buy commits, but on Nike's futures calendar the SS28 buy closes around the month the Australian range would land and line-lock precedes it by a year. The read can only steer SS29, and the Australian product must be committed before it proves anything - so the proving-ground mechanism, which is the entire reason this is separate from OPP-02, does not function. The commercial detail is worse than the market story: AUD 79.99 sits above every observable Australian point - Rebel clears roughly AUD 31-70, the UV Woven was found at AUD 44.99, the DNA 8 in discounted to AUD 34.99 from 59.99, and the NBL Store's league-partner Champion shorts top out at AUD 61.95. A premium ask into a promotional door on a seasonally INVERTED calendar (Sep-Feb against Northern Hemisphere SS delivery) with a 3-5 SKU buy split four ways is a markdown event with no statistical power to learn from. The differentiator is occupied too: AS/NZS 4399 already contemplates wet and stretched testing and Australian brands already market UPF 50+ 'wet or dry'. And '+25 percent since 2022' straddles a documented break in the AusPlay series on a count that is at-least-once-a-year and 47 percent informal. Keep it as OPP-02's first market on the existing garment at the existing AUD 69.99, not as its own slot.
scores.biggest_risk: Inventory and price risk on a buy too small to read: a premium-priced, single-market, 3-5 SKU range landed on an inverted seasonal calendar into a door whose observable ceiling is below the ask, with no reorder path and no ability to steer the buy it was justified by. Add a partnership block - iAthletic holds Basketball Australia and Champion holds the NBL - so the women's-colourway platform and the on-court cultural surround the brief leans on are not available to Nike.

scores.rationale: This is the highest-inventory-risk shape available to a merchandising planner and it is the reason it ranks below its adjusted confidence of 39. A dated, explicitly non-replenishable capsule at USD 55-85 with no carryover and no reorder path is, by construction, a terminal-markdown instrument: if it misses, there is no second season to sell it into. It lands on a shelf where the USD 65 DNA already clears at 25-50 percent off and where its own event-adjacent anchor is discounting in its moment year (USMNT replica short USD 55 to USD 44 with a code). Scalability is a 1 because the brief says so itself - not a franchise, not replenishable, does not carry units. Two things keep it out of REJECT. The rights question, which the brief called its highest-value unknown, resolved in its favour: Nike is FIBA's official product partner across apparel, footwear and equipment with the 2027 World Cup named, so DOHA sits inside existing rights. And a full-price story is genuinely scarce in a +1 percent unit business - adidas grew apparel 35 percent currency-neutral on World Cup demand in the very quarter its basketball fell 21 percent (A04-S3). But the challenger found a Nike-specific disconfirmation the brief never looked for: Paris 2024 was Nike's worst Olympic quarter on record with product in 8,000-plus doors, which converts 'dated moments pull full price' from a mechanism into a rights-and-marketing-dependent hypothesis. Then the calendar half collapses - the FIBA agreement expires in 2027 with no renewal found, LA28 merchandise and venue retail belong to Fanatics, Ralph Lauren is Official Outfitter, FIBA 3x3 apparel belongs to FOURTEEN from 2026, and licensed LA28 Mitchell & Ness swingman shorts already fill the fan-bottom occasion two years early. So roughly 20 percent of the channel mix and the entire VALLEY leg are rights Nike does not hold. WATCH, gated on two zero-cost internal reads: did the Paris 2024 and 2023 World Cup basketball BOTTOMS clear at markdown, and will a merchant place a non-replenishable FA27 capsule. Clean answers move DOHA alone back to EXPLORE; a markdown history moves it to REJECT.
scores.biggest_risk: Terminal markdown on undated-able inventory. A non-replenishable dated capsule priced above a discounting inline ladder, inside a rights position that expires the same year it ships, with a documented Nike precedent of an event capsule underperforming - and with the fan-bottom occasion already occupied by a licensed competitor. Strip the date and the challenger is right that the product content is OPP-01 plus OPP-02 plus OPP-07/08, i.e. I would be buying duplicate inventory against demand three other briefs already claim.

scores.rationale: Lowest confidence in the portfolio at development (34) and after challenge (24), three fatal kills, and the weakest evidence stack in the file - six moderate items, one weak, not a single strong. As a product programme I reject it, and the pricing is why I reject it rather than park it. EUR 45 is presented as a new mid-core rung, but the challenger's read is that if Nike's live European price is EUR 52-58 then EUR 45 is a DE-RATING of business Nike already has - permanent margin destruction dressed as market entry - and the '1.5x the KICKZ stock short' arithmetic is built on the wrong comparator, since KICKZ's EUR 29.95 TEAM25 is the entry rung, not the core. Below it sit Li-Ning's Wade clearing at EUR 20 from EUR 49 and Decathlon's own-brand Tarmak SH500 at GBP 5.99 - and a European retailer's own brand is a more durable kind of price pressure than a tariff-exposed import. The differentiator inverts: the EU withdrew the substantiation instrument (Green Claims, June 2025) and kept the prohibition instrument (EmpCo), and under a prohibition regime silence is compliant and free, so the regulation produces a floor every competitor can stand on, not a moat. And this is the portfolio's clearest duplication: OPP-03 and OPP-02 already carry the wash-durability standard, the claims demotion, the wholesale-first channel logic, the UV claim and UK/Germany/France as markets. A duplicate at lower confidence should rank below its originals, not beside them - buying both means buying inventory twice against one pool of demand. The genuinely valid content is not a product: the EmpCo legal review is time-critical at roughly three weeks out and must happen regardless, and the geographic hole - Europe is Nike's second geography and the primary market of exactly zero signals in this base - is real and independently reproduced by the auditor. Route both to the research-gap register, not to a line slot. I am also not paying EUR 120-200k for panel access plus EUR 90-140k of testing to originate demand evidence that does not exist.
scores.biggest_risk: Setting a European price rung below Nike's own realised European price - a de-rating that is very hard to reverse and that hands margin away permanently in Nike's second-largest geography - to launch a franchise whose differentiator (a substantiated-claims posture) any competitor neutralises for free by saying nothing. Compounded by portfolio duplication: the same demand would be bought twice, once here and once under OPP-02/OPP-03.

scores.rationale: The only opportunity the challenger marked survives=false, down 52 -> 26, and the reason is the one question a merchant asks first: is it already on the order form we are proposing to build. Four converging sources say most of it is - Nike Team Sports already lists Bottoms as Shorts, Pants and Tights and Capris; BSN already carries a Nike Pro 3/4 tight as a team SKU; that tight already ships in Team Navy, Team Royal and Team Maroon; and Nike Team Sports already publishes a cross-style stock colour chart. That collapses the novelty, the colour-library moat and the 'soft micro-dealer incumbent' read at once, and Under Armour's stock team colourways close the same door from the competitor side - hence market_whitespace 1 and nike_right_to_win 2. Then the engineering spec is aimed at the wrong pair: NFHS regulates SHORT-to-PANT and JERSEY-to-TIGHT, not short-to-tight, so the headline dE 1.0 standard and the 12-colour tight library serve a pairing no cited rule governs, and for most rosters the compliant tight is black, white or beige - already stocked, already USD 37. The price ceiling inverts on me: Nike's own stock 3/4 tight street-prices USD 26.97-32.00, BELOW the proposed USD 30-36 team NET, and a no-minimum custom supplier exists at USD 47.88, so neither the price argument nor the minimum-order switching argument holds. What I would keep, and it is not a line item: the enabling rule (2025-26 NFHS 3-4-5) is genuine, primary and independently re-confirmed, its published rationale is explicitly about uniform ORDERING, and A06-S1 is the best-evidenced signal in the entire base and survived every attack. The real residue is a gap the challenger could not close - no major-brand stock LOOSE full-length basketball game pant on the short's block, the one silhouette the rule most directly legalised - plus a merchandising page nobody built. Route it as a team-catalogue merchant ticket. One caveat I will not hide: the central kill rests on search-snippet reads of six egress-blocked domains, and a ten-minute direct look at the Nike Team Sports and BSN catalogues could move this score in either direction more than anything else in this ranking.
scores.biggest_risk: Booking incremental SKUs against demand Nike already serves. A 12-colour library across five silhouettes on a full team size run, at team-dealer net prices that sit ABOVE Nike's own street price for the nearest existing piece, is SKU proliferation with negative price cover - the classic way a bookings channel quietly accumulates slow-moving colour depth. The unresolved secondary risk the developer flagged itself and the challenger let stand: the linerless P&L is unproven, so the funding mechanism for the make upgrade is assumed, not costed.
